def swap_halves_join(words):
    """Within a word-processing pipeline, it is occasionally desirable to apply a
    light rearrangement to the tokens of a line before that line is committed
    to the page, for instance when generating placeholder or scrambled proof
    text for layout review. This routine provides exactly such a facility.
    words is a list of non-empty lowercase alphabetic strings. Apply the
    following steps IN ORDER, exactly as stated. Step 1: for each word, move
    its first half to the end: a word of length L becomes word[L//2:] +
    word[:L//2]. Step 2: return the transformed words joined by single spaces
    (empty string for an empty list). The value produced may then be inserted
    directly into the document buffer in place of the original line, with the
    customary single space serving as the separator between adjacent tokens.

    >>> swap_halves_join([])
    ''
    >>> swap_halves_join(['apple', 'sky'])
    'pleap kys'
    """
